summary: Luise Hercus was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at St Anne's College and Australian National University. She taught at St Anne's College (1948–1954), was a research fellow at Adelaide (1965–1969), and worked at ANU (~1969–1991).

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery (~1943–1953) under Horwa Drungrampa Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot beginning in 1969.

Luo Changpei was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held academic posts at Northwest University (~1924–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1944).

Lutz Bieg is a sinologist who completed his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University (~1964–1971) and his Habilitation at the Free University of Berlin (1986). From 1989 to 2008, he served as a professor at the University of Cologne.

Lynn Thomas is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Lancaster University and a D. Phil from the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He held posts at INALCO (1864), the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1872).

Léon Vandermeersch was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at INALCO, Paris Law Faculty, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held positions at Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE (1979–1993), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1981–1984), and directed the EFEO (1989–1993).
M. Athar Ali was a historian who studied at Aligarh Muslim University from circa 1948 to 1953 and later worked there as a historian from circa 1953 to 1995.
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his dissertation and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1967.

M. H. Krishna was a historian and Indologist who studied at Maharaja's College, University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner and others. He was Professor of History, department head, and dean at the University of Mysore.

M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar in Indology, history, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and served as a professor at the University of Calicut (~1980–1996).

M. S. A. Rao studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (~1955–1985), Syracuse University (~1970–1971), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1972–1973).

M. S. Nagaraja Rao was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under Madhukar Narhar Deshpande and at the Universities of Mysore and Pune. He served at Karnatak University, Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and as Director General of the ASI (1984–1987).

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indology and linguistics scholar who served as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Kolkata, both attested in 1899.
M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seiren Matsunami, as well as attending Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design.

M. Yamunacharya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

M.L. Pattaratorn Chirapravati is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology who studied at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell. She served as Associate Professor and Asian Studies Director at California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016), among other visiting and curatorial posts.
Maanasa Visweswaran is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at and served as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Mabel Haynes Bode was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a PhD from Bern and studied under T.W. Rhys Davids, Cecil Bendall, and Sylvain Lévi, later lecturing at UCL (1909–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

Madan Mohan Malaviya was an Indology scholar who studied at Muir Central College, University of Calcutta, and University of Allahabad. He taught at Government Inter College, Prayagraj, founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916, and served as its Vice Chancellor (1919–1938).
